decisions.title: A very brief possession
decisions.situation: A soap bubble floats past your nose. You reach for it. Your new favourite thing has already resigned.

result.title: Plenty of vacancies
result.body: There are more bubbles. You spend several happy minutes failing to keep any of them.

journal.text: I chased soap bubbles and caught absolutely nothing.

decisions.title: The two-headed jacket
decisions.situation: You manage to zip two jackets together. They are now one enormous jacket with four sleeves. This may be your greatest invention.

choices.label: Investigate whether a third one would fit
Leave your invention on the floor

result.title: Back to two jackets
result.body: You work out which zip goes where. Both jackets survive the experiment.

journal.text: I worked out how to separate two jackets I had zipped together.

decisions.title: Urgent correspondence
decisions.situation: You draw a letter and slide it into a cardboard box. It comes straight out of the missing bottom. The postal service is extremely fast.

choices.label: Fold a bottom for the box
Make a pile for each colour

result.title: Delivery delayed
result.body: The letter stays inside this time. You open the box to make sure it arrived.

journal.text: I repaired my cardboard postbox so letters would stay inside.

decisions.title: Price check on your dignity
decisions.situation: In a quiet shop, you loudly announce that Finn has a bottom. Several shoppers appear to know already.

choices.label: Repeat it for anyone who missed it

result.title: Full coverage
result.body: Finn finishes shopping at record speed.

journal.text: I made a loud announcement about Finn in a shop.

decisions.title: Imaginary friend wanted
decisions.situation: Emil is alone at break. They say their imaginary friend has moved to a better school. They are interviewing replacements on the empty part of the bench.

choices.label: Pretend you have accidentally sat on one

result.title: A crowded bench
result.body: You reject the first applicant for imaginary biting. Emil rejects the second for actually being a dragon. You run out of break before making an appointment.

journal.text: I helped Emil interview replacements for an imaginary friend.

decisions.title: Secrets bingo
decisions.situation: For indoor break, Emil makes bingo cards out of everyone’s embarrassing habits. Your square says “cries at cartoons”. They beg you not to add their baby nickname.

choices.label: Make everyone write their own square
Give a fake sob every time your square comes up
Announce their baby nickname to the room

result.title: Voluntary humiliation
result.body: You admit that cartoon dogs get to you. Someone else confesses to eating a paper cupcake case. Emil quietly removes half the original cards.

journal.text: I turned Emil’s secrets bingo into a game of voluntary confessions.

decisions.title: Forty-two. Definitely forty-two.
decisions.situation: Emil starts a question and your hand shoots up. You have an excellent answer. You are still waiting to hear what the question is.

choices.label: Let someone else risk it first

result.title: A useful last-minute adjustment
result.body: The question is about the number of sides on a triangle. You quietly retire forty-two and give the correct answer.

journal.text: I waited to hear a whole classroom question before answering.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Finn plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Finn.

journal.text: I listened to Finn’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Finn finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Ask to keep the recording private

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Finn remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Finn.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Emil secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Emil deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Emil delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: Little Star, big photograph
decisions.situation: Your school-photo proof arrives. You wore an old top that barely fits. Across your chest, in extremely clear letters, it says “LITTLE STAR”.

choices.label: Ask for a crop above the lettering
Sign the proof like a celebrity
Inspect everyone else’s proof for worse outfits

result.title: Now a very large head
result.body: The cropped proof removes the slogan and most of your shoulders. You approve it before anyone suggests keeping the original as a wallet photo.

journal.text: I cropped an embarrassing slogan out of my school photograph.

decisions.title: Fun fact about yourself
decisions.situation: You must introduce yourself with one fun fact. The person before you announces they once swallowed a coin. Everyone turns to you expecting escalation.

choices.label: Give your name and disappoint them
Claim you only eat paper money
Recite your entire biography at speed

result.title: No coins were harmed
result.body: You say you like music. A perfectly ordinary fact survives in a room briefly obsessed with swallowing things.

journal.text: I gave a simple introduction after someone set an alarming standard.

decisions.title: Your stand-in has a meeting
decisions.situation: To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. Finn is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

choices.label: Step out and take over the discussion
Leave a second dummy to play Finn
Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it

result.title: A noticeable improvement in posture
result.body: Finn says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.

journal.text: I replaced a dummy during Finn’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Finn one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Finn seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Finn I would.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Berlin, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Berlin.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Say you need a short break

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

choices.label: Save a copy and label it

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Finn remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Finn also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Step back and let them stop it

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Berlin takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: Help has been offered
decisions.situation: Someone offers a hand with a small practical task. You are not sure you need the help, but you notice yourself preparing a defence before considering the offer.

choices.label: Accept if the help would be useful
Politely decline and explain your preference
Treat the offer as an insult

result.title: A task shared
result.body: You take the useful part of the offer without treating it as a judgement on everything you can do.

journal.text: I accepted useful help with a small task.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: You are almost in the picture
decisions.situation: An old photograph catches you at the edge of the frame, apparently concentrating on something outside it. You can no longer remember what seemed so important.

choices.label: Write down what you do remember
Build a grand explanation around the pose

result.title: A life outside the frame
result.body: You let the unknown detail remain unknown. The photograph still holds an ordinary moment worth keeping.

journal.text: I enjoyed an old photograph without solving every detail.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Berlin needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Berlin.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent headaches and dizziness. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €20.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Change your position and relax your shoulders

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: What do you do all day?
decisions.situation: A stranger assumes you are retired and asks whether you have taken up “something gentle, like birdwatching”. You have not told them anything about your life.

choices.label: Tell them what your days actually involve
Say the birds are frightened of you
Describe every activity they failed to imagine

result.title: An overdue factual check
result.body: You give a short answer. They apologise for inventing your schedule before learning your name.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger’s assumption about my daily life.

decisions.title: A number with nowhere to go
decisions.situation: You suddenly remember a telephone number you have not used for years. You cannot remember what you entered a room to fetch, but the number is perfect.

choices.label: Return calmly to the original task
Treat the distraction as a personal crisis

result.title: An impressive useless recital
result.body: You repeat the number once and laugh at the timing. Memory has supplied an answer to a question nobody asked.

journal.text: I remembered an old telephone number at an unhelpful moment.

decisions.title: Older than bread
decisions.situation: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.

journal.text: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: It cannot have been this bad
decisions.situation: You revisit a comedy you have called your favourite for years. Ten minutes in, a man falls into a bucket for the fourth time. You appear to have remembered a much better programme.

choices.label: Work out what you used to enjoy

result.title: The bucket loses a fan
result.body: You stop watching without trying to defend your younger self in court. There are other ways to spend the evening.

journal.text: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.
